checks: Different groups never share cache entries even with identical initial account/header snapshots; repeated requests in one group hit its own cache
Same-URL personalized static responses stay isolated for A/Alpha, B/Beta and ordinary Chrome; managed network responses and synthetic hits do not overwrite ordinary cache
Editing, disabling and restoring group Header rules invalidates old variants before use, without changing B or ordinary requests
Login POST and Cookie changes invalidate prior identity content; another group and ordinary login/cache remain unchanged
No-store, no-cache, max-age=0, Vary:*, expired Age, Set-Cookie and Clear-Site-Data responses are never reused
Expired resources go back to network instead of serving stale data
State-changing POST invalidates cached content even when the server keeps the same login Cookie
A response started before a Header switch cannot populate or replay into the new cache generation
Vary response headers are checked against each current request, including Referer variations
Compressed UTF-8 script bodies and binary/image responses replay correctly on cache hits
Cached script execution can make synchronous XHR without deadlock; API/fetch requests are always sent to the network
Native tabs in one group share its warm cache without borrowing another group or the Profile cache
Browser-internal redirects retain the source group account/Header and do not affect B or ordinary tabs
Batched concurrent request rules preserve each group Cookie/Header for identical URLs, with ordinary requests unchanged
Cookie domain indexing preserves duplicate-name ordering and updates replacement/expiry without changing scope
privacy: Synthetic localhost accounts/headers only; no real credentials or user cache keys recorded
